keywords.rule: Counts are papers whose title or abstract contains one of the keyword's phrases (porter-stemmed, as the theme trends); the baseline is the papers in scope first submitted in the 12 weeks before the issue, its own papers excluded. new: fewer than 5 baseline papers; rising: at least 5 papers and a rate at least 1.5 times the baseline rate; hot: at least 15 papers (and 1% of the issue) at a rate at least 0.67 times the baseline rate; steady: otherwise.
keywords.score: log2(1 + n) · log2(1 + (n + 3) / (E + 3)), E = issue papers × (baseline papers with the phrase + 0.5) / baseline papers

keywords.name: Anatomy-Aware Segmentation
keywords.about: Anatomy-aware pseudo-labels, dose steering, and clinical benchmarks target segmentation and diagnosis across organs.

keywords.name: Diffusion and Flow Models
keywords.about: Diffusion and rectified-flow models are steered for style transfer, counting, molecule design, and mode-collapse analysis.

keywords.name: Lesion Detection
keywords.about: Lesion prototypes and miss-driven prompting improve retinopathy grading and small-metastasis detection.

keywords.name: Vision-Language Models
keywords.about: VLMs and MLLMs are probed for agentic failure, token repair, duration perception, and hallucination-resistant reasoning.

keywords.name: Gaussian Splatting
keywords.about: Dynamic and second-order Gaussian splatting reconstructs scenes, robots, and ultrasound volumes efficiently.

keywords.name: Robot Manipulation
keywords.about: Agents learn manipulation from execution knowledge and world-action models, probing test-time steering and reward hacking.

keywords.name: Frozen Encoders
keywords.about: Frozen foundation encoders support closed-form classifiers, medical explanations, and captioning with stabilized reinforcement learning.

keywords.name: LLM Safety
keywords.about: Safety is evaluated and restored in reasoning-tuned and streaming models, with structured harm assessment.

keywords.name: Ultrasound
keywords.about: Ultrasound papers handle domain adaptation, haze removal, novel-view synthesis, and torsion detection.

keywords.name: Multimodal Reasoning
keywords.about: Process reward models and visual credit assignment ground multimodal reasoning and calibrate abstention.

themes.name: World-Action Models and VLA Robot Policies
themes.summary: The papers develop vision-language-action policies and world-action models that predict future observations or states to guide robot manipulation, driving, and aerial control. Some contributions focus on world-model architectures and representations, while others improve policy learning, robustness, memory, and adaptation from demonstrations or failures. Several papers contribute benchmarks, datasets, and evaluation methods for these embodied models.

themes.name: Benchmarking and Evaluating LLMs, VLMs, and MLLMs
themes.summary: The papers introduce and audit benchmarks and evaluation protocols for language and multimodal models, spanning formal mathematics, code and security, document extraction, video and spatial reasoning, chemistry, and multilingual or dialectal competence. Several works diagnose evaluation validity, such as shortcut proof depth, source clustering in sampling, grader dependence, and confidence calibration for routing decisions. Others propose scoring, judging, and adaptation methods to make model assessment more reliable across safety, trustworthiness, and generalization.

themes.name: Clinical Medical Imaging AI and Agents
themes.summary: The papers develop generative, segmentation, detection, and agentic reasoning methods for clinical medical images across CT, MRI, ultrasound, pathology, and multimodal benchmarks. They differ in focusing on privacy-aware synthesis and reconstruction, robust segmentation and domain adaptation, diagnostic benchmarks and datasets, or LLM/MLLM agents that select tools and reason over evidence.

themes.name: LLM Agent Safety and Multi-Agent Reliability
themes.summary: These papers diagnose and mitigate failure modes of tool-using and multi-agent LLM systems: communication and routing breakdowns in message-passing graphs, information loss between agents, security downgrades during autonomous recovery, poisoning of self-evolving defenses, and unsafe behavior in reasoning-tuned models. Some works build attribution-focused benchmarks and controlled environments that isolate a single cause of failure, while others propose defenses such as obligation-preserving recovery, co-evolved safe disclosure, evolving secure-coding principles, and anomalous-feature erasure against prompt injection. They differ in whether they measure limits or repair them, and span single-agent, vision-language, and ecosystem-scale settings.

themes.name: Diffusion and Flow Generative Modeling
themes.summary: The papers investigate diffusion and flow-based generative models across vision, language, and scientific applications, spanning efficient generation through sparse attention, quantization, and distillation; training-free guidance, style injection, and steering; and analyses of guidance and decoding behavior. They differ in whether they contribute accelerated systems, theoretical or empirical understanding of guidance and sampling, or task-specific adaptations such as reconstruction, planning, counting, and clinical dose prediction.

themes.name: RL Post-Training and Reward Modeling
themes.summary: The papers study reinforcement-learning post-training and reward-based optimization for generative and multimodal models, comparing policy learning with best-of-N or test-time selection. They analyze what post-training actually teaches, identify reward-hacking and retention failure modes, and propose process reward models, credit assignment, and distillation methods to improve stability and reliability.

themes.name: Physics-Informed Neural Networks and Operators
themes.summary: The papers develop physics-informed neural networks and operator-learning surrogates that embed governing equations, boundary relations, or known physical structure into training. They also explore probabilistic and Bayesian formulations, symbolic equation discovery, and gradient estimation through hard switches in hybrid simulators. They differ mainly in application domain and in how physical constraints are enforced.

themes.name: Efficient Adaptation and Merging of Pretrained Models
themes.summary: The papers explore parameter-efficient adaptation through low-rank, orthogonal, closed-form, and agentic weight-editing approaches, alongside model merging through regrouping, recovery-aware task weighting, and learned manifold connectivity. They differ in whether they target a single pretrained model or combine specialist experts, and in whether adaptation is learned, statistical, or produced by an LLM agent.

themes.name: Privacy and Robustness in Federated and Distributed Learning
themes.summary: The papers study privacy and robustness risks in collaborative and distributed learning, including Byzantine vulnerability under intermittent participation, differential privacy for policy optimization and graph data, and auditing or removing learned information through unlearning. They differ in whether they analyze participation-induced robustness, design privacy-preserving mechanisms, or evaluate deletion and backdoor removal, with applications spanning federated optimization, retrieval-augmented generation, skill sharing, and language models.

themes.name: Sparse Feature Interpretability and Stability
themes.summary: These papers study how sparse and polysemantic features arise in neural representations and how to make them more interpretable and controllable. They span predicting which sparse-autoencoder features are stable, disentangling polysemantic features into monosemantic concepts, and training sparse codes across layers to predict one another. Others use neuron-level interventions, representation-similarity bounds, and weight-space probing to diagnose and steer model behavior.

themes.name: Data Stream Forecasting and Drift Detection
themes.summary: The papers develop forecasting and drift-handling methods for streaming and database settings, including online autoscaling predictors, relational pretraining, sparse in-context adaptation, and sequential change-point tests. They also introduce benchmarks for concept-drift detectors and covariate-novelty robustness in time-series foundation models. Differences lie in whether the contribution is a deployable forecasting system, a model-adaptation or testing method, or an evaluation framework.

themes.name: Dynamic and Efficient Gaussian Splatting
themes.summary: The papers extend 3D Gaussian Splatting across dynamic scenes, robotics, aerial mapping, medical imaging, avatars, and scattering media. They differ in whether they focus on compact temporal encoding, faster or second-order optimization, hybrid representations for surfaces and media, or task-specific rendering.

highlights.title: What Does RL Post-Training Teach Text-to-Image Models? A Skill-Wise Analysis of Flow-GRPO
highlights.why: Skill-wise analysis reveals Flow-GRPO's benchmark gain is sharpening on most skills but unlocking on spatial relations, overturning a single-number interpretation.
highlights.key_result: Flow-GRPO lifts the GenEval score of SD3.5-M from 0.63 to 0.95, but the paper shows the gain differs by skill: on four of GenEval's six skills, where 32 base samples already solve almost every prompt, the gain is sharpening, while on spatial relations it is unlocking, with pass@32 rising from 0.69 to 1.00 and 128 base samples not matching one post-trained sample. The benchmark average, 31 base samples per post-trained sample, describes no skill; relations carry 35% of the gain; of the other 65%, selecting among 8 base samples with the judge behind the reward recovers nine tenths.
evidence: Reinforcement learning (RL) post-training has become a standard way to improve text-to-image flow models: Flow-GRPO lifts the GenEval score of SD3.5-M from 0.63 to 0.95, a gain read as the model having learned compositional generation.

On four of GenEval's six skills, where 32 base samples already solve almost every prompt, the gain is sharpening: one post-trained sample is worth 4 to 10 base samples, and pass@32 barely moves. On spatial relations it is unlocking: pass@32 rises from 0.69 to 1.00, 128 base samples do not match one post-trained sample, and prompts the base model never solved in 32 samples are solved 93% of the time, as often as those it solved. The benchmark average, 31 base samples per post-trained sample, describes no skill. Relations carry 35% of the gain; of the other 65%, selecting among 8 base samples with the judge behind the reward recovers nine tenths.

highlights.title: Understanding Mode Collapse in Diffusion Models under Classifier-Free Guidance
highlights.authors: Daniel Pfrommer, Chenyang Yuan, Frank Permenter et al.
highlights.why: Derives analytic closed-form solutions showing how classifier-free guidance causes mode collapse and concentration, offering much-needed theoretical understanding.
highlights.key_result: The paper derives analytic closed-form solutions for the guided distribution at all noise scales and guidance levels, for a model where the conditional distribution is a Gaussian mixture whose means lie on an ellipsoid and the unconditional distribution is a single Gaussian. The analytic solution shows that classifier-free guidance induces (a) a shift along a mean-axis direction and (b) a persistent skew toward, and concentration around, a singular point corresponding to the conditional sample starting from zero noise, which the authors validate on pretrained, large-scale image diffusion models.
evidence: We propose an analytical model to capture this observation: the conditional distribution is a Gaussian mixture whose means lie on an ellipsoid, and the unconditional distribution is a single Gaussian approximating the mixture. The flows arising from this mixture are closed under scaling, enabling us to derive analytic closed-form solutions for the guided distribution at all noise scales and guidance levels.

Our analytic solution shows that classifier-free guidance induces (a) a shift along a mean-axis direction and (b) a persistent skew toward, and concentration around, a singular point corresponding to the conditional sample starting from zero noise. We validate our theoretical predictions on pretrained, large-scale image diffusion models.

highlights.title: FORK: Co-Evolving Safe Disclosure and Decision Skills Against Attackers Who Read Every Refusal
highlights.authors: Hieu Man, Chao Shang, Rui Dong et al.
highlights.theme: LLM Agent Safety and Multi-Agent Reliability
highlights.why: Co-evolves guardrail decision and disclosure skills against adaptive attackers who read every refusal, cutting adaptive ASR while preserving utility.
highlights.key_result: Averaged over three agents on FORK-World, FORK cuts attack success rate (ASR) under adaptive attack from 78.4% to 14.1% and keeps utility above 85%, outperforming baselines on both ASR and utility. Notably, on MT-AgentRisk, whose environments and tasks are unseen in training, FORK lowers ASR from 70.6% to 9.1% with 93.1% benign utility.

highlights.title: SEEK: Self-Evolution through Execution Knowledge for Agentic Robot Manipulation
highlights.authors: Zeyang Guan, Qihao Zhao, Rui Gong et al.
highlights.theme: World-Action Models and VLA Robot Policies
highlights.why: Proposes an agentic framework that retains execution knowledge as self-evolving programmatic policies so robots improve across deployment attempts without model retraining.
highlights.key_result: SEEK retains execution knowledge across attempts with a fixed underlying model: on RoboDojo, knowledge retained over ten attempts raises SEEK's average task score from 27.0 to 54.4 and its success rate from 19.7% to 48.0% across all 42 tasks, and with GPT-6.2 Astra on 34 of these tasks SEEK reaches 80.1 after five attempts against 49.6 for the model acting directly while using 77.6% fewer model requests.
evidence: On RoboDojo, knowledge retained over ten attempts raises SEEK's average task score from 27.0 to 54.4 and its success rate from 19.7% to 48.0% across all 42 tasks.
On 34 of these tasks with GPT-6.2 Astra, SEEK reaches 80.1 after five attempts, against 49.6 for the same model acting directly, and uses 77.6% fewer model requests.

highlights.title: How Many Samples Is RL Worth? Best-of-N versus RL Post-Training for Text-to-Image Models
highlights.why: Directly measures the best-of-N to RL exchange rate for text-to-image models with human labels, showing RL is especially valuable on positional prompts.
highlights.key_result: Over all prompts, our primary test, which we fixed in advance, finds best-of-16 with the VLM picker 9.3 points behind one RL image when both automatic judges must pass an image.
evidence: Over all prompts, our primary test, which we fixed in advance, finds best-of-16 with the VLM picker 9.3 points behind one RL image when both automatic judges must pass an image.

highlights.title: CypherMAS: Benchmarking Routing Reliability in LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems
highlights.authors: Danil Kostromin, Andrey Sakhovskiy, Semen Budennyy
highlights.theme: LLM Agent Safety and Multi-Agent Reliability
highlights.why: Isolates routing and communication in fixed multi-agent graphs against known optimal paths, revealing communication reliability as a distinct scaling bottleneck.
highlights.key_result: Across eleven open-weight models from 4B to 753B, the paper shows that small models fail at routing and tool use, dense models above 27B degrade with diameter, and successful runs exceed minimum LLM calls.
evidence: Across eleven open-weight models from 4B to 753B, small models fail at routing and tool use, dense models above 27B degrade with diameter, and successful runs exceed minimum LLM calls.

The results show that small models fail at both routing and tool invocation. Larger models maintain high success rates across chain, star, bipartite, and ring graphs, but success declines as the diameter of the graph increases. Successful CypherMAS runs may exceed the theoretical minimum number of LLM calls and the effect of communication mode on this overhead is model-specific.

highlights.title: JetDiffusion: Pushing the Speed Limits of Video Generation with NVFP4 Sparse Attention
highlights.authors: Yulun Wu, Zihan Min, Minshen Zhang et al.
highlights.why: Combines trainable sparse quantized attention and staged distillation training to achieve 273x video generation speedup without quality loss, a systems contribution with immediate practical value.
highlights.key_result: At 90% sparsity, VSQA accelerates attention by 8--29x compared with FlashAttention on different hardwares. On Wan2.1-14B, the resulting model achieves 273x end-to-end video generation speedup on the RTX 5090 while maintaining comparable video quality.
evidence: At 90% sparsity, VSQA accelerates attention by 8--29x compared with FlashAttention on different hardwares.
On Wan2.1-14B, the resulting model achieves 273x end-to-end video generation speedup on the RTX 5090 while maintaining comparable video quality.

highlights.title: Best-of-$N$ Test-Time Steering Can Lead to Reward Hacking in Vision-Language-Action Models
highlights.authors: Vanshaj Khattar, Jing Liu, Toshiaki Koike-Akino et al.
highlights.theme: World-Action Models and VLA Robot Policies
highlights.why: Shows best-of-N test-time steering can systematically reward-hack under verifier error in VLA policies and proposes calibration-based mitigation.
highlights.key_result: The paper shows that best-of-N test-time steering of VLA policies is vulnerable to inference-time reward hacking when the verifier is imperfect: with controlled errors in the verifier's simulation, larger N widens the gap between predicted and clean reward and can erase the gains of a perfect verifier while increasing safety violations. For the frypan placement task with output noise, increasing N from 5 to 75 raises predicted reward from 0.1189 to 0.1957, while the clean reward of the same selected actions falls from 0.00356 to -0.00135.
evidence: In this paper, we show that best-of-N test-time steering of VLA policies is vulnerable to inference-time reward hacking when the verifier is imperfect. With a perfect verifier, increasing N improves safe task completion, but with controlled errors in the verifier's simulation, larger N widens the gap between predicted and clean reward and can erase these gains while increasing safety violations.

For the frypan placement task with output noise, increasing N from 5 to 75 raises predicted reward from 0.1189 to 0.1957, while the clean reward of the same selected actions falls from 0.00356 to -0.00135 (Figure ).

news.title: Verifiable Social Reasoning for LLM Assistants
news.summary: Google Research introduced an evaluation framework built on multi-agent social simulations in which a target agent with a hidden motive interacts with other agents, including one representing the user, who then consults the evaluated assistant to infer that motive, providing verifiable ground truth by construction. Testing diverse LLMs in this setup, the authors report that user mediation substantially complicates social reasoning, that models are sensitive to user framing and require more detail than humans to reach correct predictions, and that they fail to fully leverage clarification questions; the framework and dataset are open-sourced.

news.title: How to Optimize NVFP4 Attention on NVIDIA RTX Blackwell Through Register Recycling
news.summary: NVIDIA describes an optimized SageAttention3 NVFP4 attention kernel for RTX Blackwell (SM120) that splits each N128 score tile into two N64 register slots and recycles registers after softmax quantization, overlapping the next tile's QK computation with the current tile's remaining operations. The schedule improves NVFP4 attention kernel latency by up to 1.64x on the RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, and Reactor integrated it into its production serving stack for world models with end-to-end latency reductions of up to 15.34% across LongLive, Helios, OmniDreams and Cosmos 3 Nano workloads; the core optimization was merged into the FlashInfer main branch.

news.title: Where scientists draw the line on AI agents
news.summary: A Hugging Face tech report describes interviews with 17 scientists in the natural, applied and social sciences about the responsible development of AI agents, covering where they would accept agentic assistance, what could go wrong and what safeguards they would need. The authors identify five dimensions of scientific trust (validation, privacy, objectivity, accountability and transparency) and argue scientists should help decide which tasks agents take on, how they operate and how their performance is evaluated.

news.title: An Indic Voice Agent with CUGA
news.summary: Hugging Face describes a small Indic voice agent built on CUGA, IBM Research's open-source agent harness, acting as a farm assistant that answers spoken questions in the user's language from a 154-page English agricultural handbook in two to four sentences and shows the source pages. The authors report that CUGA's default English-only embedding model retrieved the wrong passages for Hindi or Tamil queries, fixed by using intfloat/multilingual-e5-large, and that speech is handled by Sarvam AI cloud APIs or open-source SraVaani and Svara models.

themes.name: 世界-动作模型与 VLA 机器人策略
themes.summary: 这些论文开发视觉-语言-动作策略和世界-动作模型，预测未来观测或状态以指导机器人操作、驾驶和空中控制。一些贡献侧重于世界模型架构和表示，另一些则改进策略学习、鲁棒性、记忆以及从演示或失败中的适应。若干论文为这些具身模型贡献基准、数据集和评估方法。

themes.name: 对 LLM、VLM 和 MLLM 的基准测试与评估
themes.summary: 这些论文引入并审查了语言和多模态模型的基准与评估协议，涵盖形式数学、代码与安全、文档抽取、视频与空间推理、化学以及多语言或方言能力。若干工作诊断评估效度，如捷径证明深度、采样中的来源聚类、评分器依赖以及路由决策的置信度校准。另一些工作提出评分、评判和适应方法，使模型评估在安全性、可信度和泛化性方面更可靠。

themes.name: LLM 智能体安全与多智能体可靠性

highlights.title: Understanding Mode Collapse in Diffusion Models under Classifier-Free Guidance
highlights.authors: Daniel Pfrommer, Chenyang Yuan, Frank Permenter et al.
highlights.why: 推导出解析闭式解，揭示无分类器引导如何导致模式坍缩与集中，提供亟需的理论理解。
highlights.key_result: 论文针对一种模型推导出所有噪声尺度和引导级别下引导分布的解析闭式解，其中条件分布为高斯混合、其均值位于椭球上，无条件分布为单一高斯。解析解表明，无分类器引导会引发 (a) 沿均值轴方向的平移，以及 (b) 朝向并集中于一个奇异点的持续偏斜，该奇异点对应于从零噪声开始的条件样本；作者在预训练的大规模图像扩散模型上验证了这一点。
evidence: We propose an analytical model to capture this observation: the conditional distribution is a Gaussian mixture whose means lie on an ellipsoid, and the unconditional distribution is a single Gaussian approximating the mixture. The flows arising from this mixture are closed under scaling, enabling us to derive analytic closed-form solutions for the guided distribution at all noise scales and guidance levels.

Our analytic solution shows that classifier-free guidance induces (a) a shift along a mean-axis direction and (b) a persistent skew toward, and concentration around, a singular point corresponding to the conditional sample starting from zero noise. We validate our theoretical predictions on pretrained, large-scale image diffusion models.

highlights.title: FORK: Co-Evolving Safe Disclosure and Decision Skills Against Attackers Who Read Every Refusal
highlights.authors: Hieu Man, Chao Shang, Rui Dong et al.
highlights.theme: LLM Agent Safety and Multi-Agent Reliability
highlights.why: 共同进化护栏决策与披露技能，以对抗会读取每次拒绝的自适应攻击者，在保持效用的同时降低自适应 ASR。
highlights.key_result: 在 FORK-World 上对三个智能体取平均，FORK 将自适应攻击下的攻击成功率（ASR）从 78.4% 降至 14.1%，并将效用保持在 85% 以上，在 ASR 和效用上均优于基线。值得注意的是，在 MT-AgentRisk（其环境和任务在训练中未见）上，FORK 将 ASR 从 70.6% 降至 9.1%，良性效用为 93.1%。
evidence: Averaged over three agents on FORK-World, FORK cuts attack success rate (ASR) under adaptive attack from 78.4% to 14.1% and keeps utility above 85%, outperforming baselines on both ASR and utility. Notably, on MT-AgentRisk, whose environments and tasks are unseen in training, FORK lowers ASR from 70.6% to 9.1% with 93.1% benign utility.

highlights.title: SEEK: Self-Evolution through Execution Knowledge for Agentic Robot Manipulation
highlights.authors: Zeyang Guan, Qihao Zhao, Rui Gong et al.
highlights.theme: World-Action Models and VLA Robot Policies
highlights.why: 提出一种智能体框架，将执行知识保留为自进化的程序化策略，使机器人在部署尝试中无需模型重训练即可改进。
highlights.key_result: SEEK 在底层模型固定的情况下跨尝试保留执行知识：在 RoboDojo 上，十次尝试中保留的知识将 SEEK 在全部 42 个任务上的平均任务得分从 27.0 提高到 54.4，成功率从 19.7% 提高到 48.0%；而在其中 34 个任务上使用 GPT-6.2 Astra，SEEK 在五次尝试后达到 80.1，直接行动的模型为 49.6，同时模型请求减少 77.6%。
evidence: On RoboDojo, knowledge retained over ten attempts raises SEEK's average task score from 27.0 to 54.4 and its success rate from 19.7% to 48.0% across all 42 tasks.
On 34 of these tasks with GPT-6.2 Astra, SEEK reaches 80.1 after five attempts, against 49.6 for the same model acting directly, and uses 77.6% fewer model requests.

highlights.title: How Many Samples Is RL Worth? Best-of-N versus RL Post-Training for Text-to-Image Models
highlights.why: 直接测量了文生图模型在用人工标签时 best-of-N 与 RL 的兑换率，表明 RL 在位置提示上尤其有价值。
highlights.key_result: 在所有提示上，我们预先固定的主要测试发现，当两个自动评判器都必须通过一张图像时，使用 VLM 选择器的 best-of-16 比一张 RL 图像落后 9.3 分。
evidence: Over all prompts, our primary test, which we fixed in advance, finds best-of-16 with the VLM picker 9.3 points behind one RL image when both automatic judges must pass an image.

highlights.title: CypherMAS: Benchmarking Routing Reliability in LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems
highlights.authors: Danil Kostromin, Andrey Sakhovskiy, Semen Budennyy
highlights.theme: LLM Agent Safety and Multi-Agent Reliability
highlights.why: 在固定多智能体图中，对照已知最优路径分离路由与通信，揭示通信可靠性是一个独特的扩展瓶颈。
highlights.key_result: 在从 4B 到 753B 的十一个开放权重模型上，论文表明小模型在路由和工具使用上失败，27B 以上的稠密模型随直径增大而退化，成功运行超过最低 LLM 调用次数。
evidence: Across eleven open-weight models from 4B to 753B, small models fail at routing and tool use, dense models above 27B degrade with diameter, and successful runs exceed minimum LLM calls.

The results show that small models fail at both routing and tool invocation. Larger models maintain high success rates across chain, star, bipartite, and ring graphs, but success declines as the diameter of the graph increases. Successful CypherMAS runs may exceed the theoretical minimum number of LLM calls and the effect of communication mode on this overhead is model-specific.

highlights.title: JetDiffusion: Pushing the Speed Limits of Video Generation with NVFP4 Sparse Attention
highlights.authors: Yulun Wu, Zihan Min, Minshen Zhang et al.
highlights.why: 将可训练的稀疏量化注意力与分阶段蒸馏训练相结合，实现 273x 视频生成加速且不损失质量，是具有直接实用价值的系统贡献。
highlights.key_result: 在 90% 稀疏度下，VSQA 在不同硬件上将注意力加速 8--29x（与 FlashAttention 相比）。在 Wan2.1-14B 上，所得模型在 RTX 5090 上实现 273x 端到端视频生成加速，同时保持可比的视频质量。
evidence: At 90% sparsity, VSQA accelerates attention by 8--29x compared with FlashAttention on different hardwares.
On Wan2.1-14B, the resulting model achieves 273x end-to-end video generation speedup on the RTX 5090 while maintaining comparable video quality.

highlights.title: Best-of-$N$ Test-Time Steering Can Lead to Reward Hacking in Vision-Language-Action Models
highlights.authors: Vanshaj Khattar, Jing Liu, Toshiaki Koike-Akino et al.
highlights.theme: World-Action Models and VLA Robot Policies
highlights.why: 表明在 VLA 策略中，当验证器存在误差时 best-of-N 测试时引导会系统性地 reward-hack，并提出基于校准的缓解方法。
highlights.key_result: 论文表明，当验证器不完美时，VLA 策略的 best-of-N 测试时引导容易受到推理时 reward hacking：在验证器模拟中存在受控误差的情况下，更大的 N 会扩大预测奖励与干净奖励之间的差距，并可能消除完美验证器的增益，同时增加安全违规。对于带输出噪声的煎锅放置任务，将 N 从 5 增加到 75 会使预测奖励从 0.1189 升高到 0.1957，而相同所选动作的干净奖励从 0.00356 下降到 -0.00135。
evidence: In this paper, we show that best-of-N test-time steering of VLA policies is vulnerable to inference-time reward hacking when the verifier is imperfect. With a perfect verifier, increasing N improves safe task completion, but with controlled errors in the verifier's simulation, larger N widens the gap between predicted and clean reward and can erase these gains while increasing safety violations.

For the frypan placement task with output noise, increasing N from 5 to 75 raises predicted reward from 0.1189 to 0.1957, while the clean reward of the same selected actions falls from 0.00356 to -0.00135 (Figure ).

news.title: Verifiable Social Reasoning for LLM Assistants
news.summary: Google Research 推出一个基于多智能体社交模拟的评估框架，其中具有隐藏动机的目标智能体与其他智能体交互，包括一个代表用户的智能体，用户随后咨询被评估的助手来推断该动机，从而在构造上提供可验证的真值。在此设置下测试多种 LLM 后，作者报告称用户中介显著增加了社交推理的复杂性，模型对用户表述方式敏感，并且需要比人类更多的细节才能得出正确预测，同时未能充分利用澄清性问题；框架和数据集已开源。

news.title: How to Optimize NVFP4 Attention on NVIDIA RTX Blackwell Through Register Recycling
news.summary: NVIDIA 描述了针对 RTX Blackwell (SM120) 优化的 SageAttention3 NVFP4 注意力内核，该内核将每个 N128 分数 tile 拆分为两个 N64 寄存器槽，并在 softmax 量化后回收寄存器，使下一个 tile 的 QK 计算与当前 tile 的剩余操作重叠。该调度在 RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell 上将 NVFP4 注意力内核延迟最多降低 1.64x，Reactor 已将其集成到世界模型的生产服务栈中，在 LongLive、Helios、OmniDreams 和 Cosmos 3 Nano 工作负载上端到端延迟最多降低 15.34%；核心优化已合并到 FlashInfer 主分支。

news.title: Where scientists draw the line on AI agents
news.summary: Hugging Face 的一份技术报告描述了与 17 位自然、应用和社会科学领域科学家关于 AI 智能体负责任开发的访谈，涵盖他们会在哪些方面接受智能体协助、可能出现的问题以及他们需要哪些保障措施。作者确定了科学信任的五个维度（验证、隐私、客观性、问责制和透明度），并认为科学家应帮助决定智能体承担哪些任务、如何运作以及如何评估其表现。

news.title: An Indic Voice Agent with CUGA
news.summary: Hugging Face 描述了一个基于 CUGA（IBM Research 的开源智能体框架）构建的小型 Indic 语音智能体，充当农场助手，用用户语言回答来自 154 页英文农业手册的口头问题，以两到四个句子作答并显示来源页面。作者报告称，CUGA 默认的仅英语嵌入模型在印地语或泰米尔语查询中检索到错误段落，通过使用 intfloat/multilingual-e5-large 修复；语音由 Sarvam AI 云 API 或开源 SraVaani 和 Svara 模型处理。
